name: Deepnote
long_description:
Data science is as much a scientific and creative process as it is an engineering one. It involves working together, failing, learning and going back to the drawing board. Data scientists are explorers. To make data projects successful, we need tools that are both powerful and easy to use. Tools that help us collaborate and share our work in an engaging way. Tools that make data science fun again.

At Deepnote, we’re building a new standard in data tooling — a notebook that brings teams together to explore, analyze and present data from start to finish.

We are building tools for explorers. Join us.

news.title: Deepnote raises $20M for its collaborative data science notebooks – TechCrunch

launches.title: Agent Initiative Benchmark: build the best proactive agent on the market
launches.body:
Hey folks,

Jakub here from Deepnote (YC S19). Most folks in the current YC batch are building something with agents (and increasingly, proactive ones). Over the past two months, my team has benchmarked models across a carefully curated synthetic company to determine which model is best.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=128744&key=user_uploads/1275/4f647900-64d4-439b-ba2f-685a8f1dead6)

Today, we’re introducing the Agent Initiative Benchmark. It tests 12 frontier models on realistic workplace tasks inside a synthetic company  with 6 highly detailed years of history. It includes a financial model, CRM records, Linear tickets, and real-life events that affect company development, like competitor product announcements or the SVB collapse.

We used the company’s Slack to test how a proactive agent listening in on each conversation would help the team with day-to-day tasks: from stepping in to align initiatives across teams to warning the team not to use an unapproved customer logo.

What we found:

1. Two OpenAI models, GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, beat Anthropic’s latest, Claude Fable 5.2.
2. The most expensive models aren’t the best: the three priciest finished 3rd, 4th and 5th. Fable 5.1 costs 430x more than GPT-6 Luna and scores only 1.1 points higher out of 10.
3. The labs’ models behave differently: Anthropic has the three fastest models, with good-enough answers, while OpenAI’s models take the top two scores and are the cheapest at every quality level.
4. Grok 4.7 and Gemini 4 Argon are overthinkers. They averaged 35 tool calls per task, hit our 3-minute limit without a useful answer in 1/3 of their runs, and scored the lowest.
5. Models help even when they’re not needed: 11 of 12 did it at least twice in our 10 no-action tasks. This failure costs 80% more than staying silent. It is a critical problem for proactive agents and is unsolved across providers.

If you’re building a proactive agent, our research team at Deepnote is happy to partner with you on benchmarking. If you’d like to do it yourself, we’re open-sourcing the benchmark code and the synthetic dataset.
